title: Measures to Protect Bus Drivers and Public Transport Service Staff
what_it_is: Measures to Protect Bus Drivers and Public Transport Service Staff

sections.label: Zero tolerance for abusing transport workers
sections.summary: The Government, unions, operators and most Singaporeans are united in a zero-tolerance approach to abuse of public transport workers, with LTA to raise commuter awareness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Government, unions, public transport operators, and I would say the great majority of Singaporeans, we stand united in taking a zero-tolerance approach towards such abusive behaviours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For the small number who think they can behave badly and get away with it, let me be clear – if you abuse our public transport workers, whether verbally or physically, be prepared to face the full consequences under the law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA will work with the unions and public transport operators to remind commuters of the serious consequences of abusing public transport workers and to raise awareness on the responsibilities of commuters on public transport.

sections.label: Queensland bus driver safety review
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether LTA or MOT will explore reviews like Queensland's 2018 Improving Bus Drivers' Safety Review, which introduced anti-shatter films, driver barriers and a passenger code of conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My question is: will LTA or MOT be willing to explore doing reviews just like what was done by the state of Queensland, Australia, for example, where they did an Improving Bus Drivers' Safety Review in 2018?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They came up with a few measures introduced in 2018, including anti-shatter films, driver barriers and also a release of a code of conduct for passengers in the middle of 2018.

sections.label: Resuming protective shield trials on buses
sections.summary: The Union is working with public transport operators to resume trials of protective shields on public buses, addressing shortcomings from a 2018 trial involving LTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Union is currently working with the respective public transport operators to resume trials on installing a protective shield on our public buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since the Senior Minister of State asked what other suggestions we may have, we aim to address the feedback and shortcoming surfaced in a previous trial in 2018, which the LTA was involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This suggestion from the unions is currently being discussed with the operators.

sections.label: Glare from protective shields
sections.summary: The speaker says feedback will be gathered, noting previous trials showed protective shields caused glare that affected drivers and bus captains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think that is a very key consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will also get their feedback, because I think previously the trials showed that when you put some of these protective shields in place, there was a bit of glare that affected the drivers, the bus captains.
